- When sentiment history shows a recent spike (e.g., 1.00), model tends to overreact — forecast overshoots true price, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.  
- Model consistently underestimates price peaks in the 3rd–5th day of the forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or low.  
- Model overestimates later days (e.g., 15–30) when sentiment is neutral — true price often pulls back or stabilizes, suggesting mean reversion.  
- If last 3–5 days of history show downward trend, model tends to forecast higher than true — correct by reducing forecast slope.  
- When sentiment is 0.25 or above, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior day’s forecast.  
- Model fails to capture “late breakout” patterns — true price often rises sharply after 20–25 days, but model lags by 1–3 days.  
- If sentiment history is all 0.00 for 5+ days, model should not assume upward momentum — forecast should be conservative, close to recent mean.
